hard_spots.why_hard: 坊や is used repeatedly to and of a child stated to be a girl (p2 女の子). Literal 'boy / sonny' would mislead English readers about sex; neutralising to 'baby' loses period usage. Needs consistent policy plus margin note, not silent resolution.

Potato is hard, gritty ざくざく, tasteless, as if frozen 凍ったかのやうに. Must stay literal and faintly unpleasant before it is anything; English will want to explain it as symbol of poverty or psychology. The detachment (心が淋しくうつむく) happens inside the mouthful without commentary.

Long looping sentences of abstract nouns:善や悪や、かなしみや苦しみ怒りもなやみも、よろこびも; なつかしみと許し; 安らかさ / 安息. Who the three are, when this day is (old age, death, time itself), and whether 安息 is religious must not be clarified. English pressure to vary synonyms, ennoble, or call it heaven/premonition/daydream must be resisted; keep plain repetition.

うまうまうまうま with spoon banged down while looking at mother. Onomatopoeic yummy-yummy babble, not lexical sentence. Transcribe effect without making child articulate; keep physical simultaneity with mother's 坊や call.

Author glosses: 卓テーブル, 怜悧れいり, 微笑ほほゑみ, 茫然ぼんやり, 希のぞみ etc. in historical kanaづかひ. Readings fix sense (テーブル as table, ほほゑみ as smile). English cannot show ruby; do not italicise into exoticism. 卓 vs テーブル shift and food vessels (茶碗, 土瓶, アルミ鍋, 藍色の深い鍋) carry poor-household period texture to keep concrete.

Ending refuses arc:箸をおいた, resolve to work and rise early, child put to breast falls asleep mid-feed, room goes still, man stands still and whispers 嵐だな. No moral, no consolation gloss. Must allow eternal and next morning to sit side by side; last line only weather, echoing p1 and p19 without symbolism.

motifs.english: Keep one plain English set throughout and repeat, not vary: quiet / quietly for 静か, restful / restfulness for 安らかさ, rest/repose for 安息. Same vocabulary for evening, mother's manner, and vision so table and eternity share language. Do not lift into lyricism or religious peace.
motifs.why: Connective tissue binding supper, memory and vision; fluent English will vary into calm/peaceful/serene/still and destroy network.

motifs.english: Keep far / distant / far-off for 遠い, not remote/removed/estranged. Preserve spatialising of time: future seen through bottom of eyes as distant picture.
motifs.why: Marks mother's detachment: gaze, heart and future all go far. Ordinary usage made deliberate by recurrence; unifies potato moment and vision.

motifs.english: Keep silently / without speaking for 黙って, not wordlessly/tacitly in variation. Her silence is plot: husband asks twice why she is quiet.
motifs.why: From shared smiling silence at table to trance silence to unreported vision; must track as same word.

motifs.english: Keep smile / smiling for 微笑, 笑ひ, ゑみ, ほほゑみ as one field; allow smile overflowed / held back as text has it. Same smiles on parents and on vision figures.
motifs.why: Tenderness and vision share lexis: parents' helpless overflowing smiles and the three figures' continuous quiet smiles. Varying into grin/beam delights would break link.

motifs.english: Keep weariness, sadness, suffering (and trouble/anguish なやみ where present) as fixed equivalents and keep lists long with and…and. Do not compress lists or substitute hardship/pain synonyms.
motifs.why: Recurrence across body, memory and vision is the argument: same burdens at table, in past three years, and inside endless story. Text power is accumulation, not striking phrase.

motifs.english: Keep fond remembrance (or nostalgic fondness if chosen) for なつかしみ and forgiveness for 許し as paired fixed nouns wherever they occur; never paraphrase into nostalgia/pardon/reconciliation variants.
motifs.why: Paired nouns on which whole vision turns; past suffering remembered as なつかしい夢, future all turned into なつかしみと許し. Destroying repetition destroys crux.

motifs.english: Keep storm for 嵐 and sound of rain-wind for 雨風の音 as sound heard, forgotten, heard again. Do not turn into symbolism or pathetic fallacy; weather simply goes on outside.
motifs.why: Frame: p1 heard, p8 unheard through bustle, p19 quietly heard in silence, p38 whispered when still. Must remain arc of sound.

motifs.english: Keep drifting markers as at some point / before she knew it / suddenly for いつか, いつとなく, ふと without firming into she realised / she imagined. Preserve soft transitions where present, memory and future soak into one another.
motifs.why: Medium of story: she slides rather than decides; she feels as if grown old over three years. Signposting would rationalise consciousness that experiences time as unbroken telling.

motifs.english: Keep three years / only three years / only a little while as literal arithmetic shock, repeated plainly. Do not inflate into years of hardship moral.
motifs.why: Felt lifetime versus counted three years is pivot from vision back to resolve to work; repetition carries hope that is not improvement but distant holding.

narration.english_tense: Past as default for supper and memory, allowing the vision's gnomic present-future (p17 過去るであらう…変る事だらう) to stay timeless without shifting whole text into present. Do not use historical present to enliven domestic opening or to signal meditation as important.
narration.frame: Single evening: outside the door a storm; inside a narrow room under a dim lamp hanging by the wall, young parents and plump baby at table for supper. Narration begins jointly on couple watching child, narrows almost imperceptibly via potato into mother, stays mostly inside her drifting attention, returns to shared dialogue and closing tableau of clearing, nursing, stillness, weather.
narration.narrator: Third-person literary narrator, close and gentle, starting omniscient-joint then settling near the mother without explicit interior marking; often leaves who-sees and when soft. Vision never reported to husband; husband's questions and plain answers stay outside it.
narration.person: third person, sliding focus from couple to mother
narration.tense_habits: Japanese mixes てゐた progressive-past and た completion with nonpast/gnomic だらう in reflection; stative weariness and continuing smiles rendered as ongoing states. Historical kana and ruby aid reading but do not change tense. English should allow long looping and… and… sentences and slow lists to pool, not shorten into crisp modern periods.
timeline: p1: outside door, already dark, violent rain-wind, storm
p2-p9: supper begins; baby gripping table snatches so bowls/pots moved underneath leaving spoon and small plate; noisy happy feeding in snatches; storm forgotten
p10-p13: mother serves beef/onion/carrot/potato from dark-blue pot, tastes gritty tasteless potato as if frozen; heart turns lonely, recalls poor sad three married years as dreamlike

p14-p18: arithmetic (only about three years) versus feeling grown old; drifting into dim picture of three quiet people heads together over endless story, smiling unmoving, wrapped in remembrance/forgiveness/rest
p19-p20: husband asks why silent (first time); she starts, cannot say it, hears storm quietly, holds thought that day of remembrance/forgiveness/rest after long life/sadness/suffering exists

p21-p32: husband asks again; she answers only banal startling fact of short marriage and vague great hope; he answers it won't be much longer, child will walk; baby cries うまうま, fed; chopsticks laid down
p33-p38: resolve to work, rise early tomorrow; child put to breast falls asleep cheek to breast; room still; man stands still and whispers storm

data.say: Hold vision unlocated and diction plain; let eternal and next morning sit side by side. Repeat abstract nouns, do not explain potato or husband, do not end on moral.

style_sheet.annotation_density: Sparse. Annotate only what sentence cannot give: 坊や usage for a girl, aluminium pot / dark-blue pot period poverty without picturesque gloss, historical kana/ruby where sense depends on gloss, baby babble. Never annotate what context supplies; never use note to resolve vision's three figures or day into heaven/old age/death.
style_sheet.author_voice: Taisho literary prose, gentle slightly formal but plain in its own terms; power in accumulation and recurrence, not striking phrases. Allow long looping sentences and slow lists of everything life contains. Tenderness rendered physically (cheek pinched, rice pushed into two mouths, cheek to breast) not named grandly. Do not ennoble food or poverty, do not coarsen husband's warmth, do not lift vision into lyric consolation.
style_sheet.honorifics_and_names: No surnames or given names in text; do not invent. Keep kin labels as common nouns (father/mother/husband/wife) where narrator uses them. For 坊や do not use Boy/Sonny; use baby / little one with margin note on period generic, pending editor decision, and keep consistent. No Sensei or honorifics to preserve. Name order not applicable.
style_sheet.keep_in_japanese: Nothing kept in Japanese in reading view except defended need: transcribe baby うまうまうまうま as uma-uma with note rather than translating yummy, if editor allows; otherwise plain yummy-yummy babble. Food 御飯 as rice, 茶碗/土瓶/鍋 as bowls/pots in English; do not leave Japanese vessels untranslated.
style_sheet.quotation: Japanese uses 『』 for direct speech (きかない奴だな, どうして黙ってるの, 坊や, うまうま, etc.) and embedded thought/独言. Render direct speech in English double quotes, baby babble likewise, with plain dialogue tags. Do not add said-softeners or resolve unattributed speakers where text leaves soft.
style_sheet.register: Narrator: plain gentle literary slightly formal, past-default, long periodic where Japanese loops. Husband speech rough-edged warm masculine colloquial (なァ, 俺たち, 奴, 独言-like strength) without dialect costume or archaism. Wife speech soft feminine period polite (ませんのね, んですものね, ませうね) audible as feminine-polite, not coy. Baby: noise, not lexis.
style_sheet.ruby_and_italics: Ruby gives reading/nuance: 卓テーブル, 怜悧れいり, 微笑ほほゑみ, 茫然ぼんやり, 希のぞみ. Follow gloss sense (table, perspicacious, smile, blankly, hope) in English body; do not italicise or footnote ruby itself unless sense genuinely ambiguous. Italics reserved for emphasis present in sense, not for foreignism.
